name: dhun-workspace
description: Entry points for the DHUN web workstream. This manifest declares no dependency and runs no install: it exists so that 'the web app' has one command for each thing a person wants to do, without anyone having to remember which directory the tool lives in. The application itself is app-web/ and has its own manifest.

scripts.check: npm run check:icons && npm run build && npm test && npm run check:docs

comments.dependencies: None, and none is planned. The app ships no runtime dependency; adding one would change what app-web/tools/build.mjs and scripts/test_app_web.py assert, so it is a decision rather than an install. The website has its own manifest (website/package.json) and its own toolchain.
comments.check: 'check' is the web workstream's local gate. It is not the whole repository gate — the Kotlin/Android/desktop work is verified by CI (see .github/workflows/ci.yml) and cannot run in this sandbox.
